rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis A is an infectious disease that affects the liver.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: UKHSA states that most people recover within six months, although serious liver disease can occur rarely.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: Vaccination and good hygiene are identified as the main preventive measures.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: The virus is present in the faeces of an infected person and can contaminate hands, food and surfaces.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis A spreads readily between people.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: Symptoms listed by UKHSA include fever, flu-like symptoms, sickness and jaundice.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: UKHSA provides public-health management guidance and recommendations for pre-exposure immunisation.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: The guidance collection includes factsheets, contact-immunisation material and information resources for schools and parents.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: Hepatitis-A risk depends on exposure route, hygiene, food or water contamination, immunity, vaccination, setting and timing.

rows.source: UKHSA hepatitis-A prevention and control
rows.verified: UKHSA hepatitis-A evidence is person-, contact-, food-, setting-, vaccine-, intervention- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: FSA food-hygiene guidance covers cooking, cleaning, chilling and avoiding cross-contamination.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: Food businesses are expected to manage food safety using appropriate hygiene controls.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: FSA guidance includes specific material on E. coli cross-contamination.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: Food businesses must provide allergen information for prepacked and non-prepacked food and drink.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: Food businesses must handle and manage food allergens effectively during preparation.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: Allergen controls should address labelling, communication and cross-contact.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: Effective cleaning is an important control for reducing allergen cross-contact.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: Precautionary allergen labelling should only be used where an unavoidable cross-contamination risk cannot be sufficiently controlled.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: Food-safety risk depends on product, process, time-temperature control, hygiene, cross-contact, staff practice and consumer susceptibility.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency food hygiene and allergen controls
rows.verified: FSA evidence is food-, process-, business-, consumer-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level illness probability.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: The Yellow Card scheme accepts reports about suspected medicine side effects and medical-device adverse incidents.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Anyone can report a suspected problem through the Yellow Card scheme.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Reports can include injury or near injury caused by a broken, mislabelled or misused medical device.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Treatment interruption or an incorrect diagnosis caused by a device can be reportable.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Suspected defective, poor-quality or counterfeit medicines and devices can be reported.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Medical software, apps and artificial-intelligence systems used for a medical purpose may be medical devices.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Healthcare professionals are asked to report adverse incidents involving medical software through the Yellow Card scheme.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Manufacturers must report qualifying UK medical-device incidents to the MHRA under the vigilance system.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: Medical-device risk depends on device model, software, indication, user, patient, maintenance, environment and incident circumstances.

rows.source: MHRA Yellow Card and medical-device incident reporting
rows.verified: MHRA reporting evidence is product-, incident-, user-, patient-, investigation- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level harm probability.
